answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a refundable deposit before it can trade, with the stake slashed if peers catch it misbehaving. New identities start with no reputation and must wander through low-value tasks, earning small attestations over time, before they can touch larger deals. A single actor spawning thousands of fake agents faces a real cost per identity, like a zephyr that can scatter dust but cannot move a comet: cheap fakes blow away, while established agents carry weight.
